sections.title: What is a Usage Sentence?
sections.content: A usage sentence is an example sentence that demonstrates how a word or phrase is used in context. Sentences help learners understand proper usage, grammatical patterns, and natural language flow. Sentences can be linked to one or more lemmas (with optional refinement to specific meanings or surface forms).

fields.name: Latin Transliteration
fields.description: Optional transliteration of the sentence using Latin characters. Helps with pronunciation and searchability.
fields.guidance: Use standard transliteration schemes (e.g., ISO 15919 or simplified IAST). Keep transliteration consistent with the sentence's natural flow.

fields.name: Translation
fields.description: Optional English (or other language) translation of the sentence. Helps learners understand the meaning.
fields.guidance: Provide a clear, natural translation. The translation should capture the meaning, not be a word-for-word literal translation.

fields.name: Register
fields.description: The formality level or register of the sentence (formal, neutral, informal, colloquial).
fields.guidance: Register helps categorize the sentence's context and formality level. Use 'neutral' for standard usage, 'formal' for respectful/polite contexts, 'informal' for casual speech, and 'colloquial' for regional/dialectal variations.

fields.name: Explanation
fields.description: Optional explanation or context about the sentence. These are for creators and curators only—they are not shown to learners.
fields.guidance: Use explanations to record editorial notes, cultural context, or usage clarifications. Examples: "Used in literary context", "Regional variation", "Shows polite form".

fields.name: Difficulty
fields.description: Optional difficulty level (1-5) indicating how advanced this sentence is. 1 = beginner, 5 = advanced.
fields.guidance: Set difficulty based on grammatical complexity, vocabulary level, and length. Simple sentences with common words = 1-2, complex sentences with advanced grammar = 4-5.

items.example: Entering just 'नमस्कार' instead of 'मी तुम्हाला नमस्कार करतो.'
items.solution: Use complete, grammatically correct sentences that demonstrate natural usage.

items.mistake: Using overly complex or literary sentences
items.example: Writing sentences from classical literature that learners won't encounter in daily use
items.solution: Prioritize sentences that learners will actually encounter and use in real communication.

items.example: Creating sentences without linking them to relevant lemmas
items.solution: Link sentences to lemmas to help learners see words in context. Use the Links section after creating the sentence.

items.mistake: Word-for-word translations instead of natural translations
items.example: Translating 'मी तुम्हाला नमस्कार करतो' as 'I you greeting do'
items.solution: Provide natural translations that capture the meaning, not literal word order.
